newsitem.title: USA: Southern Electronics says fundamentals sound.
newsitem.headline: Southern Electronics says fundamentals sound.

text.p: Southern Electronics Corp on Wednesday said it believes the fundamentals of its business are sound and that it will continue to seek steady growth in revenues through increased sales and business acquisitions.
The company said it was making the comments in response to to what it called a substantial decline in the price of its stock in recent weeks.

Southern Electronics chief executive Gerald Diamond said in a statement the company "is not presently aware of any material information that could reasonably be expected to adversely affect the price of our stock in the marketplace."
The stock was up 3/4 at 8-5/8 in early afternoon trading Wednesday.
Southern Electronics distributes microcomputers, computer peripheral products and cellular telephone products to value-added resellers and dealers.

Southern noted in its press release that the statements it made are forward looking and are made under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. It also noted that certain factors could cause results to differ and these factors include "the highly competitive nature of the industry and Southern Electronics Corporation's ability to continue to control both credit losses and sales, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of revenues, and to sustain careful inventory management systems."
